name: ssansi
description: THE CARD SHOWS ANSI ART AS DRAWN: SIXTEEN COLOURS ON SIXTEEN BACKGROUNDS, AND CODE PAGE 437.  With the Second Sight card in slot 3 and sscon up as ttyv3's display, the console shell runs ansicat -b 9600 on a six-row fixture (disk_src/testdata/ansi.ans) into /dev/ttyv3.  Each row is built to land one VGA attribute byte on the card, bg<<4|fg under the palette in ANSI order: bold yellow on blue $4B (bold is the bright foreground), blink on red $97 (iCE colour: the bright background), code page 437 bytes $DB $B0 $B1 $B2 $80 at 7 on 0, a 256-colour 196 folded to bright red $09 as Linux vt.c folds it, a 24-bit blue background $47, and yellow on green made the default by CSI 8 ] and returned to by ESC[0m, $23.  A ^Z and a SAUCE record follow the art, and ansicat must stop at the ^Z.  ssansi_check.py reads the card's mirror in bank $E0 at the address the module logged, row v being mirror row start_line+v, and asserts each row's bytes and attribute; it is inconclusive if ttyv3's ring never received the file.  DISCRIMINATES: with _Vt_ApplySgr folding colours to the SHR's four slots again the attributes are wrong on every row, and with Con_PutChar masking to seven bits row 2 carries ASCII letters.
